decisions.correction: Keep Ramayyan exactly as drawn: bare-headed, thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth with no border, seated on the same brown horse at frame-left, reins in one hand. At the right edge of the frame, show the front rank of the Dutch column STANDING, seen from behind or cut off by the frame edge so that no Dutch face can be read: blue coats, boots and muskets still held upright in their hands, with a clear strip of bare sand in front of their boots. decisions.correction: Draw De Lannoy in true profile facing LEFT, so his LEFT side is nearest the viewer, with the white linen bandage wrapped round his LEFT hand and wrist clearly visible on the near hand hanging at his side; his right hand is bare and mostly hidden behind his body. The small gold St Thomas cross with flared, budded arms appears ONLY on Mathoo Tharakan's chain. Varma's hair is pure jet black, with no grey, gathered in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not a bun on the crown. Nagoji's cream sleeves are down to his wrists, so no brand or scar shows. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: the composition, the granite room with one window onto green hills and drilling spearmen, Nagoji standing by the timber door in his rust-red turban and red sash, Tharakan in dark maroon silk and gold chains and Ramayyan with stylus and palm leaves on the mats, Varma seated on the low platform with the spear leaning beside him, the brass lamp, and the clear upper stone wall for the caption.

decisions.issues: The script calls for 'Tharakan, close', but v01 is a wide group shot that adds three uncast figures. decisions.correction: This is a CLOSE-UP of Mathoo Tharakan ALONE: his head and chest fill the lower two thirds of the frame, and NO other person appears anywhere (no king, no guard at the door, no bearded courtier, no figures through a window). One chain carries a small gold St Thomas (Nasrani) cross with flared, budded ends on each arm, not a plain Latin cross and not a crucifix. decisions.issues: De Lannoy is right: pale hair tied with a black ribbon, the torn, soot-stained blue coat, boots, the linen bandage on his LEFT hand, and an unbowed stride between two bare-chested spear guards. decisions.issues: Composition, setting and De Lannoy are excellent: the over-the-shoulder view, pale hair with a black ribbon, the torn blue coat, and the bandage on his correct (LEFT) hand. decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma's hair must be jet black throughout, with no grey or silver strands at the temples, in the side knot or anywhere else. Keep the rest of this composition: Tharakan seated cross-legged on the mat at left in a dark maroon silk tunic with heavy gold chains and the small gold St Thomas cross, gesturing softly with open hands; Varma seated on the low stone platform at right, chin in hand, listening; the window between them onto the yard where bare-chested Nair spearmen drill. decisions.issues: Seen from behind, De Lannoy's linen bandage is on his RIGHT wrist (the arm hanging from his right shoulder, on the frame's right side). decisions.correction: De Lannoy stands upright in the near foreground at left, seen from behind over his LEFT shoulder as in 8.4, never sitting on the floor. Show his pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon and his torn, soot-stained blue coat. The linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist only: that hand hangs at his side on the frame's left edge, nearest the camera, and his right hand is bare. Acceptable. De Lannoy matches his sheet's face and hair: pale wavy hair with a black ribbon, in the torn, soot-stained blue coat. Minor: the drill yard reads level with the room rather than below the window, and Varma sits beside the window rather than squarely framed in it. Varma matches his sheet: black hair in a knot on his left side, no turban, gold necklaces, cream-and-gold mundu. De Lannoy's bandaged left hand in the torn, soot-stained blue coat hangs in the near foreground. Bare-chested Nair spearmen with topknots drill against green hills. No painted text. decisions.correction: Varma's hair must be entirely jet black, with no grey, silver or white strands at the temple, above the ear or anywhere else. Draw it gathered into a single compact knot above his LEFT ear, as in the previous panel, with no loose mass of curls hanging down the back of his neck. decisions.issues: This is not a tight insert. It is a wide room shot with three extra figures, and Ramayyan should be the only person in the panel. A full-bearded, bare-headed man sits on the King's platform, so he reads as a wrong Varma. A heavy man in maroon sits on the mat, and a bare-chested guard with a spear stands at the door where Nagoji should be. decisions.correction: Make this a TIGHT close-up insert of Ramayyan alone. No other person appears anywhere in the frame: no King on a platform, no man in maroon, no guard or figure at the door, and no window or yard. Frame from just above his bowed, balding head with receding dark curls down to his lap. His head is lowered and turned down at the upper left, eyes on his work, never looking up. His thin, steady fingers hold the metal stylus scoring a single palm leaf resting on the bundle in his lap, lower centre. Show only fine incised lines on the leaf, nothing legible. He wears plain unbordered white cloth draped over one shoulder, with no jewellery, forehead marks or sacred thread. Behind him is only a plain, softly shadowed granite wall. Keep the upper right half of the frame that quiet, empty wall for three speech balloons.

decisions.issues: We see De Lannoy from behind: the rear coat pleats and buttons face us. So the bandaged hand on the sill, on the right side of the picture, is his RIGHT hand. Otherwise good: half-turned figure at the window, torn blue coat, pale hair with a black ribbon, open sky over green hills, and a quiet floor and wall band at the foot for the caption.
decisions.correction: The linen bandage must be on De Lannoy's LEFT hand and wrist only. Because we see him from behind, his left hand is on the LEFT side of the picture: show that left hand bandaged, hanging at his side just clear of the coat skirt. His right hand, on the right side of the picture, rests on the stone sill completely bare, with no bandage or wrapping. The drilling spearmen in the yard below are bare-chested Nair men with forward-tied topknots and white mundus, with no vests or tunics. Keep everything else as it is: De Lannoy half turned from us at the wide window, pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon, face in profile looking out, the torn, soot-stained blue coat. Keep the timber door and brass lamp at left, the green hills of Travancore under a wide open sky, and the plain floor and low wall along the foot of the panel left quiet for the caption.

decisions.issues: De Lannoy wears a long white wrap skirt with a white sash under the open blue coat, with no breeches or boots. This mixes in his later white mundu costume, which the bible starts only at page 13 panel 4, and breaks continuity with panel 2 (blue breeches and boots). decisions.correction: Below the coat, De Lannoy wears his officer's blue breeches tucked into tall black boots, exactly as in the previous panels. Draw no white skirt, wrap, mundu or sash at his waist. His white waistcoat and shirt show only at the chest under the open coat. Keep all staining to grey-black soot smudges and ash on the blue cloth, with no brown or reddish drips or spatter anywhere. Keep everything else as it is: Nagoji seen from behind in the near foreground at the timber doorframe, with rust-red turban, long curly black hair, tiny gold stud, cream tunic and red sash. Keep De Lannoy standing full-on in the torn blue coat, pale wavy hair, looking straight at Nagoji, linen bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. Keep Varma small and seated on the platform behind him by the window, bare-headed with his knot, gold necklaces and spear, and the plain granite wall above De Lannoy's head clear for the balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) fails three character rules. (1) Nagoji's ear ornaments are studs with a gold bead hanging below the lobe on both ears. That is the sheet's drop earring, which the author ruled on 2026-10-02 must be refused at selection. (2) Stubble shading darkens his chin under the lower lip and along the jaw. The commander look requires a smooth, clean-shaven chin. (3) We see De Lannoy from behind, so his right arm is on the right of the frame, and the linen bandage is on that RIGHT wrist. The bible row says LEFT hand and wrist. Minor: the blue coat has a pixelated, checkered quilt texture. What works: the over-the-shoulder reverse angle, Nagoji in the timber doorway with his hand on the doorframe in the full commander look, the window with drilling Nair spearmen, and the clear stone wall in the upper middle for both balloons.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: an over-the-shoulder view from behind De Lannoy in the left foreground (pale wavy hair tied with a black ribbon, the torn soot-stained blue coat), and Nagoji standing in the open timber doorway at right with one hand on the doorframe. He wears the commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar. Keep the single window with Nair spearmen drilling in the yard at upper left and the plain granite wall in the upper middle, clear for two balloons. Fix three things. First, Nagoji's ear ornament is a single tiny flush gold stud pressed on the lobe, with no bead, ball or drop hanging below it on either ear. Second, his chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble, hatching or dark shading under the lower lip or along the jaw; only the thick curled moustache. Third, De Lannoy's linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist only. Seen from behind, his left arm is the one on the LEFT side of his figure in the frame. His right arm, on the right side of the frame nearer Nagoji, ends in a bare hand below the coat cuff, with no wrapping. Paint the coat as plain woven blue wool with torn edges and soot smudges, not a checkered or quilted pattern.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) has three faults. (1) Anatomy: the bare hand on the right of the frame has a thumb plus five fingers with nails, which makes six digits. (2) Handedness: De Lannoy faces us, so the bandaged hand on the left of the frame is his RIGHT. The bible requires the bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. (3) The bandaged hand shows its back, with nails and knuckles, so it is not palm-up as the script asks. Its wrap is also streaked with rust-brown stains that could read as old blood. What works: the tight framing, his face above the hands looking down, Varma soft and out of focus on the platform beyond (bare-headed, black hair, gold necklaces, spear), the window with drilling spearmen, and wall space at the upper left and upper right.
decisions.correction: Keep this tight composition. De Lannoy fills the left and centre in the torn soot-stained blue coat over a stained white shirt, his face high in the frame looking down at his own hands, and both open hands are held out in the foreground. Varma sits soft and out of focus on the low stone platform at right: bare-headed, black hair in a side knot, gold necklaces, spear leaning behind him. Both hands are turned PALMS UP, so we see the palms and finger pads, never the nails or knuckles, and each hand has exactly one thumb and four fingers. The clean plain cream linen bandage, with no brown, rust, red or pink stains, wraps his LEFT hand and wrist. Because he faces us, that is the hand on the RIGHT side of the frame. His right hand, on the left side of the frame, is bare and unwrapped.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) breaks the Varma MUST MATCH rule: his hair is clearly salt-and-pepper, with silver-grey strands from the temples to the knot. The bible requires black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure. De Lannoy is in right-facing profile, and the only visible bandaged arm is his near arm, which is his RIGHT. The bible puts the bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. What works: the two-shot framing, with De Lannoy kneeling at left, head lifted to the King, and Varma seated at right with a smile on the gold-bordered mundu and spear. The window of drilling spearmen, the open-wick lamps and the clear upper wall and sky also work.
decisions.correction: Keep this two-shot unchanged in layout. De Lannoy kneels on the woven mat at frame-left in profile facing right, head lifted toward the King, in the torn soot-stained blue coat over a stained white shirt with pale trousers. Varma sits on the low stone platform at frame-right with a faint smile, bare-chested in the gold-bordered cream mundu and gold necklaces, spear leaning behind him. Keep the single window of drilling Nair spearmen between them and the open-wick brass lamps, and leave the plain upper wall clear for the balloons. Fix two things. Show it resting on his far knee, visible just in front of his body and wrapped in clean plain linen. His near right hand, resting on the near knee, is bare with no wrapping.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) dresses De Lannoy wrongly for this page. Under the blue coat he wears an ankle-length white mundu and sandals, the costume reserved for page 13 panel 4 onward. The bible requires the torn blue coat with boots through page 13 panel 2, and panels 3 and 5 of this page show trousers and boots. He stands three-quarter toward Varma, so the bandaged forearm across his chest is his RIGHT arm, while the bible puts the bandage on the LEFT. He also stares sideways rather than giving the slow nod. What works: the wide room with the open door at left, Ramayyan seated cross-legged at centre writing with the stylus on a palm-leaf bundle, and Varma bare-headed with black hair on the platform with his spear. The window with drilling spearmen and the large clear upper wall for both balloons also work.
decisions.correction: Keep this wide composition. De Lannoy stands at left beside the open timber door. Ramayyan sits cross-legged on the woven mat at centre in plain white cloth, his stylus moving on a palm-leaf bundle. Varma sits on the low stone platform at right, bare-chested in the gold-bordered cream mundu with gold necklaces, black hair in a side knot, spear leaning behind him, beside an open-wick brass lamp. Keep the single window of drilling Nair spearmen and the plain upper wall clear for two balloons. Fix De Lannoy. His head dips forward in a slow nod, eyes lowered. The clean linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist. As he stands three-quarter toward Varma, that is the hand hanging at his side on the RIGHT of his figure in the frame. His right hand, on the left of his figure, is bare. Varma's head turns slightly toward Ramayyan in a small nod.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) shows Nagoji with his sleeves rolled to the elbow. The pale puckered brand and the long white scar sit plainly on his RIGHT forearm: he faces us, with the talwar on his left hip, so the brand is on the arm at the left of the frame. Varma's hair carries visible grey streaks at the temple, against the black-hair rule. Under De Lannoy's coat, an ankle-length white cloth reads as a mundu, though his boots are correct. What works: De Lannoy's back in the doorway with the bandage correctly on his LEFT wrist, and the two bare-chested Nair spearmen escorting him. Nagoji stands aside with a clean chin, curled moustache and a flush gold stud. Ramayyan looks up from his leaf, and Varma watches the door. The wall above Ramayyan and the sky in the door and window leave room for two balloons.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition unchanged. decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's sleeves are rolled and the brand plus white scar show on his left forearm, although 12.1 does not call for pushed-up sleeves. The beat is missed. Varma is still seated on the platform, gripping the spear, and is not rising. Nagoji is still by the far door, not at Varma's shoulder. The composition nearly repeats 12.1. decisions.correction: Stage this as a new moment, not a repeat of the previous panel. Marthanda Varma is visibly getting up, half-risen off the low stone platform with his weight coming onto his feet and his knees straightening, and his right hand closes around the shaft of his spear where it leaned against the wall. Through the window are green hills and a yard of drilling bare-chested Nair spearmen in white mundus. Varma's hair is black and gathered in one knot above his LEFT ear, not a loose mane. decisions.issues: Varma has a prominent grey streak at his temple. The bible says he must never have the grey hair of the sheet's later figure. His knot sits on top of his head and is tied with an orange band, not placed above the left ear. Minor: the Nair guards' topknots are at the back of the head, not forward-tied. decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma's hair must be entirely jet black, with no grey or silver streak at the temple or anywhere else. He is the young king here, not the grey-haired later figure on his sheet. Gather his hair in a single plain knot above his LEFT ear, with no coloured band. decisions.issues: Minor. The background courtyard is a two-storey galleried block with a stair, a little grander than the single-storey tiled quarters in 12.3. The upper-left sky band is fairly tight for four lettering areas, so the long Nagoji line may need the low-detail flagstones at the lower left. Everything else matches. The light is pre-dawn blue-grey. De Lannoy is tall with pale wavy hair and a black ribbon, wears the torn soot-stained blue coat and boots, and has the linen bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. On the stone bench by his door sit a folded white tunic-coat, a folded white mundu and sandals. Nagoji arrives across the flagstones in the commander look with his sleeves pushed up. The bandage is on the wrong hand. De Lannoy's body is turned so the near, viewer's-left arm is his RIGHT, and that is the arm wrapped in linen; the bare hand touching a button is his LEFT. The face and hair do not match the sheet or 12.4: he is a rugged older man with loose straight golden hair and no ribboned queue. The framing is a mid-shot, not a tight one. The buttons are plain brass with no letters, which is fine, and the pre-dawn courtyard and sky are good for the balloon.
decisions.correction: This is a tight close-up on De Lannoy's coat front and hands, and he is the same man as in the previous panel. He is young and clean-shaven, with pale-blond wavy hair tied back in a queue with a black ribbon, as on his sheet; he is not a rugged older man with loose straight hair. His lowered face may appear at the top edge of the frame. The linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist only, and his RIGHT hand is bare. With his body facing the viewer, the bandaged left hand rests low on the viewer's RIGHT side of the picture. The bare right hand comes in from the viewer's LEFT, and its THUMB runs down the row of plain brass coat buttons, each with a worn interlaced mark and no letters. Keep the torn, soot-stained blue coat and the pre-dawn blue-grey courtyard light. Leave clear sky or plain wall in the upper part of the frame for one long balloon.
